text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein recovers after successful prostate operation in the United States.

- Saudi Arabian billionare Prince Al-Waleed bin Talal and other investors participate in Philadelphia Bank's capital hike to 20 million ($28 million) dinars; bank manager says that bank is moving towards comprehensive banking.
- Justice Minister Riyad Shakaa says new measures to be taken to help boost the independence of the judiciary.
- Sources say parliamentary elections will be held next November with hopes of an early election receding.
- Opposition MPs preparing a memorandum on the "single vote" system.
- Eight centrist parties holding successful merger talks.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with King Hussein at a Minessota hospital ahead of talks in Washington.

- A ministerial committee to examine the new election law; acting Prime Minister Nsour says his resignation from parliament is not a move preceding dissolution of parliament and says does not rule out an extraordinary session of the chamber.
- Traffic accidents increased by 16.6 percent in 1996.
